segments.he: חוּץ מִפָּחוֹת שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה בַּקֶּרֶן כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין גְּזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת, אֲבָל גְּזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת – צָרִיךְ לֵילֵךְ אַחֲרָיו; חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא תִּיַּיקֵּר.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if the robbery victim forgave the robber concerning both payments, «excepting less than» the «value of one peruta of the principal,» he need not pursue him in order to return the remaining debt. «Rav Pappa says: They taught» that the robber is not obligated to pursue the robbery victim «only when» the «stolen item is not extant, but» if the «stolen item is» still «extant, he must pursue him» to return it, as «we are concerned» that «perhaps» the stolen item «will appreciate» in value, and the debt he owes will exceed the value of one peruta.
